clue.text: Things built by this practice are to one's specifications

definitions.text: Things built by this practice are to one's specifications

parts.words: Things built by this practice are to one's specifications
parts.note: the word for a habitual practice, put before 'built', gives the term for something made to a buyer's own order

explanation.surface: A remark that goods made this way are tailored to the buyer's requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habit or usage, and custom-built goods are made to order for one client.

clue.text: Lady hit journalist with no less force

parts.note: Una is a woman's name, as in Spenser's Lady Una
to bat is to hit a ball
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A woman struck a reporter, and kept swinging just as hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means undiminished, carrying on with its full strength.

clue.text: Sherry, originally in the wood, is most cloudy

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter is placed inside the word for the wood

parts.note: a thicket is a dense wood of shrubs and small trees

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter, where the word begins

explanation.surface: Sherry aged in a cask comes out at its murkiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickest liquid is the most turbid or opaque, the least clear.

clue.text: Swot up on surgical procedure and look after old travel writer

indicators.note: after means the word for look is placed following the letter for old
in a down clue, up means the word for swot is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to swot is to cram for an exam
OP is short for operation
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Advice to bone up on an operation and care for an elderly author of travel books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the swot word, read upwards in this down clue; 'after' sets the look word behind the old one. Marco Polo was the Venetian who described his journeys to China.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant dictated a famous account of his journeys across Asia to Kublai Khan's court.

clue.text: Grape-juice a rebel imported to make wine

indicators.note: imported says the rebel is brought inside the grape-juice word

parts.note: must is unfermented grape juice
Jack Cade led the 1450 Kentish rebellion

explanation.surface: Unfermented juice with an insurgent brought in turns into a bottle of white.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a revolt against Henry VI in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Powerful lady in a hurry to become hostess of the Boar's Head in Eastcheap

definitions.text: hostess of the Boar's Head in Eastcheap

parts.note: a mistress is a woman in authority, as over a household
quickly means with haste

explanation.surface: A commanding woman rushing to take over a famous London tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boar's Head was the tavern where Falstaff drank in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives Falstaff's tavern in Henry IV a landlady of this name.

clue.text: I got into many a quarrel —- that's despicable

indicators.note: got into says the letter I is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to picking lots of fights and calls it contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Caitiff is an archaic word for a base coward, contemptible and mean.

clue.text: Money from overseas made archbish answer

annotationWithheld.why: Money from overseas made archbish answer (8): DRACHMAE is an anagram of MADE + ARCH, so 'archbish' must split into fodder ARCH and 'bish' (slang for a blunder) as indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Money from overseas made archbish answer

clue.text: Upper-class youngster in sporting assembly rising to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole thing reads from the bottom upwards
in places the class letter and child inside the gathering word

parts.note: a meet is a gathering for a hunt or athletics
U denotes upper-class usage
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A posh child at a sports gathering climbs to the head of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts UTOT inside MEET to give MUTOTEET; 'rising' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotum is a small spinning toy, a kind of spinning top with lettered sides.

clue.text: Anxieties about politician's abilities

indicators.note: about says the worries word goes around the politician

parts.note: cares are worries or anxieties
LIB is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: Worries over how capable an MP really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means quality or capacity, so calibres are people's degrees of talent.

clue.text: Hook, perhaps, or crook

explanation.surface: Captain Hook described as a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook is a buccaneer in Peter Pan, and a thief who copies or robs is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Furtive way to enter

explanation.surface: A sneaky route inside a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear entrance gives entry, and anything back-door is clandestine or underhand.

clue.text: To put things straight, ought to express agreement

parts.note: to right a wrong is to put matters straight
ought is a variant of nought, the figure zero or letter O

explanation.surface: Saying you should set matters right and then nodding yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is a casual British word said when consenting, like okay.

clue.text: Sports display is cancelled

parts.note: show's, a show being a display, plus is
an event that is off has been called off

explanation.surface: An athletic exhibition has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to flaunt it, wearing it ostentatiously.

clue.text: Let go and follow closely, hugging west coast

indicators.note: hugging says the two words embrace the letter for west between them

parts.note: to free is to release or let go
to heel is to follow at someone's heels, as a dog does

explanation.surface: Releasing something and trailing just behind along the western shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like part of 'west coast' but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to travel without pedalling or power, simply rolling along.

clue.text: Prepare to publish a retraction for some incorrect idea

indicators.note: retraction says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting a correction ready for the press to withdraw a mistaken notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds TIDE across 'incorrect idea'; 'retraction' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors correct and revise copy so that it is ready for print.

clue.text: The ability to see a positive response in the crew

indicators.note: in says the affirmative word sits inside the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a positive reply

explanation.surface: Seeing an affirmative answer from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing rowing boat and its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is vision, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Secretly disconcerted American

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Yank was quietly flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from the public.

clue.text: The joint for a sailor without a name?

indicators.note: without says the letters for a name are removed from the sailor

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor
A plus N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A question about a nameless mariner's place of meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric or metal are joined.

clue.text: Formal shuffle of the cards

indicators.note: a shuffle mixes cards up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dignified mixing of a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Starched describes stiff, prim manners, like a collar stiffened with starch.

clue.text: Praise for Kentish fire

explanation.surface: A tribute for a blaze in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish fire is old British slang for a long rhythmic burst of clapping, first heard at meetings in Kent; it is not a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is acclaim, and Kentish fire is a sustained round of hand-clapping.

clue.text: An argument against the pursuit of victory …

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, is an argument against
a quest is a search or pursuit

explanation.surface: Someone objects to chasing after a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a triumph, the act of overcoming an enemy.

clue.text: Hypocrisy in a foreign wine-shop

parts.note: cant is insincere, pious talk

explanation.surface: Two-faced talk heard in a bar abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a Spanish or Italian bar selling wine.

clue.text: … gives rise to the same points about security

indicators.note: about says the compass points go around the security word

parts.note: the same compass point twice, S and S for south
a pawn is an object deposited as security for a loan

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, it produces identical points concerning safety.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to generate or produce, as fish lay eggs.

clue.text: Wild yarn, circulated privately

indicators.note: circulated means the letters are sent round into a new order

explanation.surface: An outlandish story passed around in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwardly means within oneself, not shown or spoken openly.

clue.text: Language student abandoning French — English taken instead

indicators.note: abandoning says the student letter is dropped from the French word
taken instead says the English letter fills the gap the student left

parts.note: Gallic means French
L is the learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A learner dropping French and taking up English as a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic tongue of Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Carpet bag found on vessel

indicators.note: in an across clue, the bag going on the vessel means it is placed after it

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge of the north-east
a bag is a catch, a haul of game

explanation.surface: A rug and luggage discovered aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet as a verb means to scold severely, as being called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelhauling was a brutal naval punishment, so the word now means to rebuke harshly.

clue.text: Forcibly remove a hooligan

explanation.surface: Throwing out a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something off is to wrench it free, and a reckless young lout is called by the same phrase.

clue.text: Run a hierarchical organisation

explanation.surface: Managing a company with ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in a stocking is a ladder in British English, and a career or social structure of rungs is also so called.
